page: Amazon Web Services r5dn.metal is a memory-optimized, bare-metal server instance. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor offering 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 768.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of memory per core. For local storage, the instance features 3600 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, and it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory performance. The server achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, PassMark CPU score, and PassMark memory score. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 4542.25 GB/sec and large block uncached write speeds at 97.97 GB/sec. Database operations are a key strength, as evidenced by a strong PassMark database score and a Redis SET operations throughput of 76.05 million operations per second. Static web serving throughput is also high at 48.73 GB/sec.

While the instance excels in memory-intensive and multi-threaded tasks, it exhibits performance limitations in specific workloads. LLM text generation benchmarks are weak for small models and poor for medium models, and there is no data available for large model text generation. This makes the server less suitable for real-time generative AI text generation, though its prompt processing speeds remain average. Given its massive memory capacity, high-speed local NVMe storage, and 100 Gbps network bandwidth, the r5dn.metal is best suited for large-scale databases, memory-intensive analytics, enterprise applications, and high-throughput web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services r5dn.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized instance designed for high-throughput workloads. It features a dedicated 96-vCPU Intel Xeon 8259CL processor, 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory, 3600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and 100 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark results show strong multi-core processing, exceptional memory bandwidth, and high database performance, with Redis SET operations reaching 76.05 million operations per second. However, the instance shows performance tradeoffs, particularly in LLM text generation where it scores in the weak to poor ranges. It is highly cost-efficient for resource-dense, memory-bound applications but less suited for generative AI inference. This server is best utilized for large-scale databases, high-performance web serving, and memory-intensive enterprise workloads.
